Detailed method

This is the sourdough focaccia, not the yeasted sheet. Currently 500 g flour, 80% hydration, 20% starter, 2.5% salt, and 0% yeast. That is 400 g water, 100 g starter, and 12.5 g salt, 1012.5 g of dough. The starter is itself 100% hydration, the same assumption used for effective hydration. The page shows 81.8% effective hydration. Currently 1 sheet of 1012.5 g. Only the starter lifts it, so the pan proof takes longer. Oil, garlic, and herbs are extra and are not in the gram total. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Starter Use 100 g of starter that is bubbly and has about doubled. That starter is part of the gram total.
  2. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 400 g water, the 100 g starter, and 12.5 g salt until no dry flour remains. At 80% the dough is sticky. Wet your hands instead of adding flour. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  3. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for about 3 to 4 hours. Give it three stretch-and-folds in the first 90 minutes. It should turn bubbly and grow by about half.
  4. Pan Oil a rimmed sheet. The default 1012.5 g uses a rimmed tray about 30 cm long and 20 cm wide. If you change the amount, use a tray sized to fit, or bake in batches. About 20 g of oil is extra and is not in the gram total. Tip in all 1012.5 g. This batch is 1 sheet.
  5. Dimple After 20 minutes, oil your fingers and ease the dough toward the corners. Cover it for 45 to 80 minutes, until it is puffy. Press oiled fingers straight down to the pan so the dimples stay open.
  6. Bake Heat the oven to 220°C (430°F). A few cloves of garlic or a scatter of herbs can go on top. Those are extra and are not in the gram total. Bake 20 to 26 minutes, until the raised parts are deep gold and the bottom is crisp.
  7. Cool Leave it in the pan for 10 minutes, then move it to a rack. The photo shows that dimpled top and the open crumb.
